terms.meaning: the shared rulebook of labels, definitions, cues and tier rules used to classify signals
the automatic step that reads each signal and assigns it labels from the codebook

sections.name: File setup, CodebookTab, TABS
sections.title: Imports and editor tab list
sections.what: Brings in icons, the codebook types and display labels. Defines the seven tabs: solutions, triggers, signal types, industries, themes, tier rules and the new-project test.
sections.why: Likely reason: sets a fixed order for the editor's sections.
sections.watch_out: Tab names are tied to data keys, so renaming a key in the data breaks its tab.

sections.name: EMPHASIS
sections.title: Emphasis options with their effects
sections.what: Defines the four emphasis choices for a codebook item (prioritise, standard, deprioritise, exclude), each with an icon and a short explanation of its effect on classification.
sections.why: Gives the user a plain explanation of what each choice does.
sections.watch_out: The explanations describe classifier behaviour, so changing that behaviour without updating them would mislead users.

sections.name: DIM_NOTE, EVIDENCE, slug, clone
sections.title: Section notes, evidence grades and helpers
sections.what: Holds the short explanation for each codebook section, the four evidence grades (C1 to C4), a helper that turns a label into a lowercase ID with dashes (capped at 60 characters), and a helper that makes a separate copy of the codebook for editing.
sections.why: Likely reason: the copy keeps edits apart from the saved version until save, and the ID rule keeps new IDs tidy.
sections.watch_out: New custom IDs come from their labels, so changing this rule changes the IDs of items created afterwards.

sections.name: CodebookEditor (part 1)
sections.title: Editor tabs, search and item rows
sections.what: The main editor. Shows a tab per section with counts, a search box, an Add button, and one row per item with an expand arrow, editable label, emphasis buttons and a delete button for custom items. Adding creates a new item marked as custom. Edits only change the draft. Part of the count line is cut off in the packet.
sections.why: Likely reason: working on a draft lets the user discard changes safely.
sections.watch_out: The draft is replaced with the saved version whenever the codebook's hash or update time changes, so unsaved edits can be lost.

sections.name: CodebookEditor (part 2)
sections.title: Item details, save and footer buttons
sections.what: The expanded panel edits an item's definition and cue words, and for solutions also its lifecycle stage and whether it can be a primary solution. The footer shows classification progress, a two-click reset, a re-run button, discard, and save. Save gives new custom items IDs from their labels and says whether classifier inputs changed.
sections.why: Likely reason: the two-click reset and the disabled re-run while changes are unsaved guard against accidents.
sections.watch_out: Saving changed definitions or cues re-classifies every signal, and progress may show only part of the work while it runs.

sections.name: TierEditor
sections.title: Tier rules editor
sections.what: Edits the rules that place each signal in Tier 1 to Tier 4: the evidence grades allowed for Tier 1 and Tier 2, minimum severity and ability to act, required quoted value at risk, decision window, a private known-route check, Tier 2 minimum research score, the recency window in days, Tier 4 grades, and whether priority items lift Tier 3 and deprioritised items cap it. Changes apply immediately. Numbers are kept inside their allowed range as they are typed.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the note that tier rule changes apply instantly.
sections.watch_out: Unticking the last evidence grade for Tier 1 or Tier 2 is ignored, so a tier cannot end up with no allowed grades.

summary: The editor for the codebook, the shared rulebook that decides how every signal is labelled and ranked.
purpose: Lets a user add, edit, prioritise, exclude and delete the labels the classifier uses, and change the tier rules, then save.
why: Likely reason: the classifier's results depend on these rules, so the editor keeps a working copy and only applies changes on save.
how: 1. Copies the saved codebook into a draft. 2. Shows one tab per section, with search, add and per-item editing. 3. Tracks unsaved changes and whether they affect classification. 4. On save, gives new custom items stable IDs and sends the draft to the app. 5. Shows classification progress and offers reset, re-run and discard.
inputs: The saved codebook, the progress of classification, the tab to open first, and callbacks for save, reset and re-run.
outputs: The editor on screen, a saved codebook draft, and calls to save, reset or re-run classification.
risks: Saving changes to definitions or cues re-classifies every signal. Resetting restores defaults for the whole workspace. Unsaved edits can be lost if the saved codebook changes underneath them. Tier 1 evidence cannot be emptied.
debug: If an edit does not stick, check that Save is enabled and that progress shows no failures. If progress stalls, check the failed and last-error text. If a custom item shows an odd ID, check how its label was turned into an ID.
